topics.title: Wristband Policy
topics.body:
• All sales are final - no refunds or exchanges.
• Only wristbands purchased through AXS are valid for entry. If you purchased from an unauthorized source or have a counterfeit wristband, entry will not be permitted.
• Wristbands must be worn securely on your wrist and cannot be slipped on or off.
• Keep your wristband on for the entire festival—it must not be removed, stretched, or tampered with, as doing so will void entry.
• To re-enter the festival on the same day, your wristband must be scanned upon exiting.
• Wristbands are non-transferable and non-exchangeable.

Lost or Damaged Wristbands?
No worries! They can be replaced one time only for the original purchaser, for a $25 replacement fee. Just head to our Box Office and they'll get you taken care of. Please bring a photo ID (or picture of the photo ID) of the original purchaser.

Please Note:

• Counterfeit or duplicated wristbands will be confiscated by security.
• This wristband policy is strictly enforced, and there are no exceptions.

Your wristband is your ticket to an incredible experience! Please treat it with care-it's a revocable license, and entry may be denied or revoked for non-compliance with festival policies or protocols. By attending the festival, you voluntarily assume all risks, including potential injury or loss of property.

topics.title: 90 Degree Guarantee
topics.body:
Hinterland's 90 Degree Guarantee allows ticket holders the option to request festival admission ticket returns for any day that is predicted to reach 90° or higher.

If on Monday 7/27 at 10am CT, the weather.gov forecast for 7/30, 7/31, 8/1, or 8/2 has a true temperature of 90° or higher for the 50240 zip code, ticket purchasers will have the option to request a return of their festival admission ticket for that day. Return requests are only available for the day/s the forecast is 90° or higher. 4-Day ticket holders can request a return for specific day/s at a rate of 1/4 of the total 4-Day ticket price.

Starting Monday, July 27 at 10:00 AM CT you will be able to complete a 90 Degree Guarantee Ticket Return Request Form at hinterlandiowa.com/tickets. To guarantee your return you must submit the form before 5:00 PM CT on Tuesday, July 28.

Eligible returns will be processed within approximately 14 days.

PLEASE NOTE:
Applies to festival admission tickets only
Camping, parking, and shuttle passes are not eligible
Tickets must have been purchased directly through AXS.com
Third-party resale tickets are not eligible

Hinterland's Commitment to Climate Awareness:
The 10 hottest years on record have all occurred in the past decade. At Hinterland, we are committed to raising awareness about climate change and its impact on our daily lives. We will continue striving to make sustainable choices, both this year and in the years ahead. Together, we can make a difference.

topics.title: Free Look Return Policy (VIPs)
topics.body:
At Hinterland, we want our premium guests to feel their extra dollars were well spent. We think you'll love what we've put together! If you don't, you have options.

All 4-Day VIP and VIP+ purchasers will have the opportunity for a "Free Look" onsite after scanning in. If you decide within one hour of scanning into the festival that you aren't satisfied with the premium amenities, you can return your ticket or downgrade to a lower level. Simply visit the VIP Concierge Tent on the north side of the premium area.

To qualify for the Free Look Return Policy, purchasers must scan into the festival grounds by 6pm on Thursday, July 30.

This policy only applies to 4-Day VIP and VIP+ festival admission tickets. It does not include camping, parking, or shuttle tickets. To qualify, tickets must have been purchased directly via AXS.com. Tickets purchased from a third-party are not eligible.

topics.title: Avoid Scammers & Buying Tickets from Unofficial Partners
topics.body:
The only tickets we can guarantee are tickets purchased directly through our official ticketing partner, AXS.com.

We are unable to facilitate or provide support to tickets purchased from a third-party website or individual.

Please be aware that scammers often try to sell invalid tickets on Facebook, Instagram, StubHub, Vivid Seats, SeatGeek, Craigslist, and Marketplace by fake accounts. Tickets purchased through third-parties will not be accepted.

topics.title: Refund and Reselling Policy
topics.body:
Hinterland is rain or shine. No refunds or exchanges. Only exceptions are the 90 Degree Guarantee and Free Look Policy for VIP.

Festival performers are subject to change or cancellation at any time without notice. Prices subject to change without notice.

The only tickets we can guarantee are tickets purchased directly through our official ticketing partner, AXS.com. We are unable to facilitate or provide support to tickets purchased from a third-party website or individual.

topics.title: Tiered Ticket Pricing
topics.body:
Festival tickets are sold in tiers — same pass type, different price. This system rewards fans who buy early with the best prices.

Each tier offers the exact same access and benefits, but lower-priced tiers sell out first.

When you buy tickets:

- You may see multiple tiers listed. Choose the lowest available tier for the best price.
- Once a tier sells out, it's marked as unavailable and prices move to the next tier.
- Tiers can change quickly based on demand.

topics.title: Allowed/Not Allowed on Festival Grounds
topics.body:
Every person, vehicle and belonging entering the festival or camp grounds is subject to a full airport-style search, which may include a magnetometer screening and/or pat-down. Information is subject to change.

These items ARE NOT allowed into the festival grounds:

NO Weapons of any sort
NO Chairs (see more on chairs below)
NO Coolers
NO Smoking
NO Glass
NO Styrofoam
NO Drones
NO Laser pointers
NO Pets (service animals are welcome, see policy)
NO Fireworks
NO Professional cameras
NO Sun tent
NO Umbrellas
NO Wagons
NO Totems
NO Outside food or beverage

These items ARE allowed into the festival grounds:

YES Refillable water bottles (empty), camelpacks (empty) - clear bottles are preferred, but not required
YES Blankets or legless chairs (see more on chairs below)
YES Backpacks, purses, bags (no larger than 18"x13"x8.5", don't need to be clear)
YES Point and click film and digital cameras (No detachable lenses, please)
YES Sunblock
YES Bug spray (The reality of Iowa summers. Do NOT forget your bug spray, people!)
YES Strollers
YES Hand sanitizer
YES Liquid IV/Gatorade type packets, must be sealed

Please note that other items may be deemed prohibited at event organizers discretion.

Chairs with legs, including camping and low-lying beach chairs, are not allowed in the festival grounds. You are welcome to bring a legless chair or blanket. If you have a medical need for a chair and would like info on how to be granted an exception through our ADA services, please email access@hinterlandiowa.com or visit our ADA Tent onsite.

Click here to see what's allowed/not allowed in the campgrounds.

topics.body:

topics.title: Lost and Found
topics.body:
There is a lost and found tent inside the festival grounds near the south entrance (see map).

All items turned into lost and found will be posted on Hinterland Lost and Found, where you can search for and claim your missing items.

If you do not see your lost item, you can create a Loss Report to notify the Guest Services team. If the item gets turned in, you will be notified.

Any lost and found items not claimed during the festival will be held for a year at the Liff storage facility and can be claimed during this time at Hinterland Lost and Found; Liff will then ship the item back to you.

topics.title: Cashless
topics.body: Activate your wristband prior to the festival and link a credit card/debit card for swift payments with all vendors by registering for cashless. This is the easiest way to pay for food, drinks, merch, and more. During the festival, order at any food, drink, or merch vendor and let them know you’re paying with your wristband. Tap your wristband, enter your PIN, and you’re done!

topics.title: HinterMarket
topics.body:
Do a little shopping at the fest! We have an amazing lineup for the 2026 HinterMarket.

American Dance Party | Lakeland, FL

We use vintage clothing along with repurposed materials to create nostalgic yet fashion-forward products. All products are made in central Florida.

Azapaza | Sioux City, IA

India imports, tapestries, festival garments, djembe drums, scarves, bags, jewelry, and incense.

Baraka | Cincinnati, OH

At Baraka, our small team travels to Asia every year in search of unique and handmade jewelry, clothing, and textiles to share at festivals. All items are handmade or hand-assembled, sourced from dozens of makers across Asia. Inventory includes brass and sterling silver jewelry, clothing including tanks, tees, dresses, skirts, and pants, and accessories including bags, wall hangings, and notebooks. Plastic-free booth; post-purchase bags are made from upcycled silk from used sarees.

Brim|Stone Hat Bar | Humboldt/Algona, IA

Custom hat boutique and studio specializing in personalized headwear where you can have your hat custom-burned and embellished.

Iowa Henna | Des Moines, IA

Henna, glitter, face/body painting, clothes, fans, and light-up toys.

KIN DSM | Des Moines, IA

Sterling silver jewelry, crystals and crystal jewelry, intentional items, and great festival additions like cute travel pouches and lip balm.

Larissa Loden | Twin Cities, MN

Jewelry, hair claws, hats, socks, and permanent jewelry.

Lucid Wood | Columbus, NE

Hand-carved jewelry using wood, antler, bone, and stone — pendants, bracelets, and earrings, all one of a kind. Also sells hand-carved animal skulls inlaid with crystals, moss, mushrooms, and LED lights, and driftwood lamps inlaid with quartz crystals. All sustainable and natural materials.

Maddy Fusco Illustration | Des Moines, IA

Various forms of original art, including originals, prints, T-shirts, and stickers.

Matt Meyung | Alexandria, KY

Handmade and CNC-engraved mixed media woodwork. Paintings on wood with fractal burning. Bourbon barrel decor.

NVision Guitars | Ankeny, IA

Handmade guitars, picks, art, apparel, and music accessories.

Permanent Collection | Des Moines, IA

Vintage letterpress art prints, cards, pennants, tote bags, coasters, and sweatshirts.

Pepper Harrow | Winterset, IA

Flower crowns, wearable florals, lavender self-care products.

Roadie Rack | Des Moines, IA / Seattle, WA

Roadie Rack is a music driven thrift store built from life on the road. We specialize in rare and authentic shirts collected from music tours around the world. Every piece has a story tied to live music culture, touring, and the communities that keep it moving.

Sad Girls Club | Seattle, WA

Latina-owned, Seattle-based slow fashion festival wear brand. Creates clothes inspired by culture, femininity, and original oil paintings translated into handmade lino-cut printed and crochet clothing/accessories including tops, purses, leg warmers, sweaters, dresses, and skirts. Available in sizes XS–4X. Uses thrifted yarn and reworked fabrics; every piece is one of a kind.

Sangüich Designs | Des Moines, IA

Sangüich is a Des Moines-based queer, Latine artist merging vibrant cuteness with bold, thought-provoking messaging. Their creative studio, Club Sangüich, serves as the home for all their visual and sonic work.Roadie Rack is a music driven thrift store built from life on the road. We specialize in rare and authentic shirts collected from music tours around the world. Every piece has a story tied to live music culture, touring, and the communities that keep it moving.

Sunny Life Hats | Lake Helen, FL

Family-run, hand-crafted hemp sun hats, satchels, organic cotton bandanas, and small-batch shea-based sunblock. All items are hand-loomed/crocheted using eco-textiles and hand screen-printed from original art. Donates a portion of proceeds to service projects including tree planting, disaster relief, ocean plastic removal, and rural health clinics.

The Dust Collective | Des Moines, IA

Vintage clothing and accessories, plus handmade goods.

Then Now Always | Orlando, FL

Engraved wooden sunglasses and leather bracelets, hand-woven blankets, original design tees, tanks, sweats, and headwear.

To Write Love on Her Arms | Melbourne, FL

Merchandise and apparel that directly funds the mental health nonprofit To Write Love on Her Arms, dedicated to presenting hope and finding help for those struggling with depression, addiction, self-injury, and suicide.

Wander & Co. | Milwaukee, WI

Social cause shop where every product benefits a nonprofit or cause. Apparel and camping accessories.

topics.title: Miniland
topics.body:
Check out Hinterland's Miniland! Curated by Des Moines' own Ramona Muse Lambert, Miniland is a creative experience for all, focused on DIY art, music, and a welcoming spot for families to gather throughout the festival.

All festival long, guests are invited to try their hand at button making, patch making, keychain construction, and contributing to our bootleg Hinterland flyer wall. All are welcome to draw on our giant inflatable bear, hop in the photobooth, and give our artist-made carnival games a whirl.

Families can find some relief in our chill zone, make a Miniland kids pass, weave rainbow loom bracelets, free draw, grab an activity bag to go, and pick up a Hinterland activity newspaper while supplies last.

You can also come visit the Miniland Stage each day for a unique mix of musical performances, unconventional instrument demonstrations, and more!

topics.title: Hiking Trails
topics.body:
Explore our new hiking trails throughout the campgrounds. With nearly 3.5 miles of beautifully wooded paths, the trails are more than just a way to get where you’re going they’re a destination all their own.

Along the way, you’ll find plenty of surprises, including covered bridges, art installations, lemonade stands, a silent disco, a disc golf course and more. The trails will be lit at night, making them easy to enjoy throughout the festival weekend. After Hinterland, the trails will remain open year-round for locals and visitors to enjoy.

We recommend wearing comfortable, closed-toe shoes so you’re ready to explore!

Dragonfly Trail
Bluegill Bend
Junebug Drive

Doe Drive
Wild Turkey Way
Goldfinch Trail

topics.title: Yoga & Sound Bath
topics.body: Join us for yoga daily (Thursday-Sunday) at 9 AM by the Campfire Stage. These Vinyasa yoga classes led by Mayce at Mindful Healing Co. will focus on connecting body with breath, relaxation, mindfulness, and letting go. After the flow, there will be a 10-15 minute sound bath during savasana to bring awareness inwards and fully immerse in the soothing sounds. All levels welcome, just bring a mat/towel & water. Follow @yogimayce on Instagram!

topics.title: Merch
topics.body: Gear up with a wide assortment of merch from Hinterland and artists. Head to our socials closer to the festival for a look at this year's Hinterland styles and trinkets!

topics.title: White Claw Hammock Hangout
topics.body: Come relax in the shaded White Claw Hammock Hangout in the camping area. Bring your own hammock or use one of ours. All ticket holders are welcome!

topics.title: Silent Disco
topics.body:
Dance it out in the woods at our Silent Disco. Located on the north side of the campgrounds by the Raccoon Run and Dragonfly Trails. It’s free for all ticket holders to participate. Open Wednesday-Sunday 12 PM–7 PM and 11 PM–3 AM.

Insider Tip: Stop by the nearby face-glitter stand and lemonade cart while you’re there.

topics.title: Sunflower Field
topics.body: Take a stroll to our new sunflower field for a great photo op or a relaxing place to enjoy the view. It is located just west of Car Camping.

topics.title: Vinyl Cup Record Store
topics.body: Shop records & more from Vinyl Cup. Located inside the festival venue and Basecamp.

topics.body: Visit the Subaru Recharge Zone near the West Entrance for car karaoke, interactive art, and a place to cool down and recharge.

topics.title: Driving & Parking
topics.body:
Directions

Hinterland is located in St. Charles, Iowa, just 30 minutes south of Des Moines.

Take I-35 to St. Charles, Iowa, then use the route assigned to your parking pass, even if your GPS suggests differently. Road closures and traffic patterns are in place throughout the festival weekend, and following festival signage will get you to your lot (or home) the fastest.

NORTH ROUTE - Exit 56
Box Office, 4-Day General Parking, Premium Parking, ADA Parking, Tent Camping, RV Camping, Rideshare/Dropoffs

SOUTH ROUTE - Exit 47
1-Day Parking, Car Camping

Exit 52 off-ramps are closed Thurs, July 30 – Sun, Aug 2.

Check-in Times
Parking lots open at 9 AM each day.

Peak Traffic Times
9AM on Thursday, 1 PM–6 PM each day, and exiting the festival each night.

Lot Entrances
4-Day General Parking - Gate C
Single Day Parking - Gate N
Premium Parking - Gate C
ADA Parking - Gate F
Box Office - Gate C

Camping in any of these lots is prohibited.

When You Arrive

Parking pass window stickers and festival wristbands are required to enter the parking lots.

Place your parking sticker on the driver’s side front windshield before you arrive, and make sure everyone in your vehicle is wearing their wristband.

Don’t have a window sticker or wristband, or did you purchase your pass after July 12? Before going to the parking lot, head to the Box Office onsite (Gate C with temporary parking) or offsite (Tuesday only at Val Air Ballroom in West Des Moines)

Reminder: Festival admission passes do not include parking and must be purchased separately.

ADA Parking
ADA Parking is located just west of the South Entrance. Please enter through Gate F and show your valid DMV issued accessible parking placard or license plate and Hinterland parking or camping pass for access to these areas. Transportation is unavailable from General Day Parking, Tent Only, and Car Camping areas. If you have any accessibility related concerns, please reach out to us at access@hinterlandiowa.com

Vehicle Re-Entry
1-Day Parking Lot – re-entry NOT ALLOWED

4-Day, Premium, ADA Lots – re-entry ALLOWED during daylight hours

Hiking Trails to Parking Lots
The festival grounds are connected by hiking trails. Closed toed shoes are highly encouraged for the walk from the parking lots to the venue. It’s a lovely stroll, but no one likes rocks in their sandals!

Always walk along the marked hiking trails. Walking along Highway G50 is NOT permitted for your safety.

Festival Grounds: Gate C, south of the South Entrance. Follow the marked trails.

Digital Shuttle Passes
Shuttle passes are digital tickets. Login to the AXS app to access. Have it ready to scan each time you enter the shuttle.

Times

The last shuttle leaves the festival grounds at 2 AM, please plan accordingly.

Don’t have a wristband, or purchased after July 12th? Before going to the festival venue entrance, head to the Box Office onsite (Gate C next to shuttle stop) or offsite (Tuesday only at Val Air Ballroom in West Des Moines).

topics.title: Getting Around & Pedicabs
topics.body:
The entire festival grounds span about 2 miles from end to end, so be prepared to walk. There are designated hiking trails between campgrounds and parking lots. Closed toed shoes are highly encouraged for the walk from the parking lots to the venue. It’s a lovely stroll, but no one likes rocks in their sandals!

Walk on the festival hiking trail (marked on the map) to get around the campgrounds and from parking to festival grounds entrances. Walking along Highway G50 is NOT permitted for safety reasons.

Pedicabs
Skip the stroll and grab a ride! Coors Light will be offering pedicab rides at Hinterland this year. Perfect for getting from the parking lot or campgrounds to the festival entrance with zero fuss. Prices start at $15, all forms of payment accepted including cash, card, Venmo, PayPal, etc. Ready to ride? Flag one down or head to a pedicab pickup spot located throughout the grounds. Pedicabs are first-come, first-serve.

topics.title: The Road to Hinterland
topics.body: Make a road trip out of your drive to Hinterland with some suggestions from our friends at Subaru.

topics.title: Code of Conduct
topics.body:
Being a welcoming community for all Hinterlanders is one of our primary goals. As a guest at Hinterland, we ask you to actively work with us to create an enjoyable and accepting atmosphere for everyone. This includes speaking up when you witness unacceptable behavior.

We have a zero-tolerance policy for harassment or discrimination of any kind, including but not limited to: race, color, national origin, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, religion, and disability status.

Offensive behavior includes, but is not limited to:

- Acts of physical assault or battery
- Verbal abuse
- Racial or ethnic slurs
- Groping, sexual assault, or unwanted sexual remarks
- Stalking
- Threatening language

Any individuals or groups found in violation of this policy may have their Hinterland pass revoked.

If you feel you've been harassed, or feel unsafe, please visit Guest Services or talk to Hinterland staff or security.

topics.title: Security & Safety
topics.body:
Hinterland works closely with local, state, and federal authorities to help ensure a safe experience for all our patrons.

Every person, vehicle and belonging entering the festival or campgrounds is subject to a full airport-style search, which may include a magnetometer screening and/or pat-down.

Please review what isn't allowed within festival and campgrounds prior to attending.

Emergency exits are positioned throughout the festival grounds and clearly marked on signage and maps.

We encourage all of our guests to familiarize themselves with the festival maps to be aware of where emergency exits and medical stations are located. Please make sure that if you need any assistance to contact our guest services and event staff security team members.

The National Weather Service will be monitoring any weather events that may occur for our specific location during the festival and we have procedures in place to react appropriately to keep all attendees safe.

Please be advised that many of the performances will include flashing and strobing lights, theatrical haze, pyrotechnics, and loud sounds. Patrons with sensitivities to these effects are advised to take necessary precautions.

Subscribe to SMS to receive onsite announcements

or

Sign up for the Hinterland SMS by texting Hinterland to 42606

topics.title: First Aid
topics.body:
First Aid tents are located throughout the festival & campgrounds and staffed by trained personnel to provide any medical aid needed. In case of an emergency, notify any staff member or our security team. When in doubt: see something, say something.

Remember:
- Drink water early and often. Stay hydrated so you can enjoy the show all day long.
- Take advantage of the shade and cooling areas located around the venue.
- Don't hesitate to ask a staff member for help. They are there to help you have fun and keep you safe.

topics.title: Nursing Area
topics.body:
You are welcome to breastfeed or pump anywhere on festival grounds. There will also be a nursing and pumping area located in Miniland.

If you have medical related items or breastmilk that requires a cooler within the festival concourse, please visit the ADA Services tent for an accessibility tag.

topics.title: ADA & Accessibility Accommodations
topics.body:
We are committed to ensuring all Hinterlanders have an inclusive and accessible experience. Please review the accommodations available below and feel free to reach out to us at access@hinterlandiowa.com with any questions.

Requesting Accommodations and Accessibility Wristbands
Guests with disabilities or a special medical need, can request these accommodations by emailing access@hinterlandiowa.com. Advance request by July 10th is recommended to ensure availability. Once you arrive, please visit the ADA check-in tent just outside of the South Entrance to finish registering and receive your Accessibility Wristband - this wristband will allow access to our available accommodations. One companion wristband is also available. Children under the age of 18 will be allowed as additional companions. There is not an accessibility ticket that needs to be purchased to utilize accommodations.

We accept requests for any of the following services:

- ASL Interpretation

- Other forms of Effective Communication (such as: live captioning, large format print/braille literature, guided tours for guests with visual disabilities, assistive listening devices, or any other accommodation not listed)

To ensure adequate time for planning, requests for these services should be made by July 10th. While we will strive to accommodate requests, we cannot guarantee fulfillment after the cutoff date. To submit a request, please fill out the 2026 Effective Communication Request Form.

Once you arrive, please check-in at the Accessibility Services Hub to be connected with our interpreting team.

Parking - Gate F
A separate accessibility parking lot is available for attendees with a valid government-issued persons with disability parking placard, permit, or license plate. For ADA parking, purchase an ADA Parking Pass at hinterlandiowa.com/tickets.

Viewing Area
An accessible viewing area with shade, small bar, folding chairs, accessible restrooms, and a water filling station is located inside the festival grounds.

Sensory Supportive Space
A tented space where sensory stimuli is more controlled for folks that may need a break or an opportunity to regulate.

Chairs
Chairs with legs are not allowed in festival grounds. However, if you have a medical need, you may bring your own from home. All chairs must have a tag from ADA Services.

Portable Toilets and Showers
Accessible portable toilets are located throughout the festival. Accessible showers are also offered (showers are available to all guests for a fee).

Charging Medical Devices
You are welcome to bring your powered medical device to ADA Services for recharging. Please note that staff are not responsible for devices left charging.

First Aid
First Aid tents are located in the festival grounds & campgrounds and staffed by trained personnel to provide any medical aid needed.

Food & Drink
Outside food or drink are not allowed in festival grounds. However, if you require special accommodation for dietary restrictions, please visit ADA Services for assistance.

Coolers
If you have medical related items or breastmilk that requires a cooler within the festival concourse, please visit the ADA Services tent for an accessibility tag.

Shuttles
The Des Moines Shuttle will have buses in rotation that have ADA accommodations and will drop off at the ADA Parking Lot.

Service Animals

Service animals are permitted throughout the venue. However, this does not include emotional support animals, therapy animals, or companion animals. Only legitimate service animals that are properly trained and under the proper care of their owners will be provided with the appropriate credentials.

The following guidelines must be followed:

• All service animals must be registered with the ADA department upon entry into the event. Please ask a security guard to call ADA upon entry.
• All service animals must remain by the handler's side at all times and must be harnessed, leashed, or tethered. If these devices interfere with the service animal's work or if the handler's disability prevents the use of these devices, the handler must maintain control of the animal through voice, signal, or other effective controls
• Service animals must be housebroken
• Anyone bringing an animal will be responsible for and liable for any damage or injury caused by the animal
• All service animals should have legally required vaccinations (which ADA staff may ask to see for verification)

topics.title: ADA Services Tent
topics.body:
The ADA Services check-in tent is located by ADA Parking, Gate F.

Staff is available here to support and address the needs of attendees with accessibility needs.

At this tent you can:
- Learn about accessibility services and receive answers to your questions
- Receive an accessibility wristband
- Receive accessibility item tags

topics.title: ADA Parking & Shuttles
topics.body:
Accessible Parking
ADA Parking provides convenient access to designated parking spaces in the ADA Parking Lot for attendees with valid accessibility credentials. To use these spaces, a valid government-issued persons with disability parking placard, permit, or license plate is required. Purchase an ADA Parking Pass.

Enter the ADA Parking Lot at Gate F.

Re-entry to the ADA Parking Lot IS allowed. Reserve your ADA Parking Pass to secure accessible parking and enjoy a smooth festival experience.

Shuttles
The Des Moines Shuttle will have buses in rotation that have ADA accommodations and will drop off at the festival.

topics.title: ADA Camping
topics.body:
Accessible Car and Tent Only Camping locations are available for guests with disabilities, as well as preferred spots within the RV campground. Please see our map for the location of the reserved ADA camping area. To camp in this area, you must have a valid government-issued persons with disability parking placard, permit, or license plate, and purchase an ADA Camping pass. There is a fixed amount of ADA camping spots in this area, so please do not purchase this pass if you do not need it on account of a disability. If you have a special medical need, it must be requested in advance by July 10th or it may not be available. You may email access@hinterlandiowa.com.

See more information on camping here.

topics.title: A Guide to Thriving at Hinterland
topics.body:
Escaping to rural Iowa's scenic landscape for 4 days of music is bound to be unforgettable, but in the anticipation of catching your favorite acts and making new friends, don't forget to make a game plan for your comfort and well-being throughout the weekend. Here's some sage advice from seasoned festival aficionados to help you make the most of your time at Hinterland.

1. Pace Yourself
It's tempting to try and do it all, but going full speed all four days is just not humanly possible. No one likes that FOMO feeling, but it's important to prioritize listening to your body if you push too hard you might have to miss a lot more than one set!

2. Recharge with Rest
While sleep might not be the first thing on your mind when you're surrounded by the festival buzz, resting once in a while goes a long way. Find a spot to take a load off for a little bit during the day or retreat to your campsite for a power nap. Earplugs and a cozy sleeping mat come in clutch for uninterrupted rest.

3. Fuel Your Adventure
Just as your car needs fuel to get you to St. Charles, your body will need nourishment to keep the good vibes flowing. Be sure to check out all the delicious eats from our food vendors. You've gotta recharge your batteries for the next dance session!

4. Dress to Impress AND for Comfort
Sprinkle in some practicality when selecting your festival styles. Think breathable fabrics, comfortable footwear, and versatile layers for adapting to changing temperatures and activities. A collapsible statement hat or funky sunglasses can elevate your look while shielding you from the sun. Stay prepared for unexpected weather changes with waterproof gear the fun doesn't stop, rain or shine!

5. Get Ready to Go the Distance
The festival grounds span about 2 miles, so be prepared to walk if you are parking or camping. There are designated hiking trails between campgrounds and parking lots. You may also want to bypass all that by buying a Des Moines shuttle pass.

6. Drink Water and Chill
Hydration is paramount for keeping your energy levels up and your spirits high, so take advantage of our new improved free water refill stations scattered throughout the festival grounds, as well as shade tents and misting stations.

7. Arrive Early, Go With the Flow
Whether you want to set up shop in the front row or you're hoping to snag a particular spot in the grounds, everyone is excited to get into the festival as soon as possible. Because of this, plan to review the maps before you leave, arrive early and be patient. Go with the flow of the line as we make sure everyone gets in safely.

8. Asking for Help is Cool
Whether you're feeling under the weather or simply need a helping hand, don't hesitate to reach out to festival staff or fellow attendees for assistance. From first aid stations to friendly faces offering directions, the Hinterland community is here to ensure everyone has a good and safe time. We're always here for you at realperson@hinterlandiowa.com.

topics.title: Camping Tips from Experienced Hinterlanders
topics.body:
How to camp like a pro and make the most of your weekend in the beautiful Iowa countryside:

1. Four words: shade and air flow. The August sun in Iowa can be a little steamy, so bringing shade canopies to cover your camping area is a worthwhile consideration. Achieve pro-level status by erecting one over your tent so you can change or nap in the daytime without melting. Clipping cloth tapestries to your canopy is a great way to keep a breeze flowing through your space while blocking the sun.

2. Spare a few minutes here and there for comfort and hygiene. It's not a backpacking trip, so you can bring a few of the creature comforts that help you stay fresh and game for a whole weekend of fun. (Check out our camping pack list for inspiration.)

Take a trip to the shower trailers for a quick refresh, and be sure to take time for tooth-brushing breaks, visits to the hydration stations, and taking care of your basic needs.

3. Stay connected by keeping your devices charged with portable batteries and chargers. It's a much smoother experience than trekking to the car to charge your phone!

4. Rain or shine, be prepared. Inclement weather can happen, so don't leave the waterproof tarps, ponchos, and rain boots at home. In case of a downpour, you'll want to keep your belongings dry by storing them in sealed plastic bags or waterproof containers.

5. Keep in mind that if you're in Tent Camping, your car will not be next to your tent. Bringing a wagon for transporting your stuff to and from the campsite is a great move.

Bonus: If you forgot something at home, swing into the Dollar General right on festival grounds.

topics.title: Hinterland for Kids
topics.body:
Each year music-loving families make their way to St. Charles for a beautiful music experience in the countryside. If you're planning to bring some little ones too, experienced festival-going parents shared a few tips to help you prepare.

1. Spend some time at Miniland
From interactive art installations to children's crafts, the corner of the festival made just for kids is ingeniously devised by Des Moines-based artist and mother of three boys, Ramona Muse-Lambert. Air conditioned and shaded, the Miniland tent is a good place for kiddos to have some quiet moments coloring and cooling off.

2. Pack the essentials
You'll want sunscreen, hats, reusable water bottles, and comfy clothing to keep the whole family happy. Make sure to remember ear protection for young children, especially if they'll be near the main stages.

3. Plan your schedule
Take a look at the festival schedule in advance as you may want to prioritize family-friendly activities and performances. Consider nap times and meal breaks when planning your day.

4. Stay hydrated and energized
With so much excitement in the air, it's easy to forget to hydrate and snack. Take regular meal and water breaks to keep everyone feeling their best.

5. Set meeting points
In case someone gets separated from your group, establish meeting points throughout the festival grounds where you can easily reunite with the fam.

If you're bringing the young ones to Hinterland, you're creating cherished memories that will last a lifetime. Grab your festival gear, round up the family, and get ready for an unforgettable experience in St. Charles!

p.s. Children 10 and under are free with a ticketed adult and do not require a wristband.

topics.title: Campgrounds Overview
topics.body:
Immerse yourself in the weekend of music by setting up camp in the friendliest corner of the Iowa countryside.

Ways to Camp
There are four different styles of camping at Hinterland:
- Tent Camping
- Car Camping
- RV
- Glamping

Find the camping option best suited for your group at hinterlandiowa.com/tickets.

Campfire Stage Access
Every festival attendee gets access to the Campfire Stage during the Campfire Stage sets.

Campgrounds Map
View the maps here.

topics.title: Check-in Times for Campers
topics.body:
Wednesday: 12 PM–8 PM

Thursday-Saturday: 9 AM–7 PM

Sunday: 9 AM–12 PM

You can NOT check in if you arrive (for the first time) outside of these hours.

Wednesday camping is encouraged! Food and drink vendors will be open.

topics.title: Restrooms & Showers in Campgrounds
topics.body:
There will be port-a-potties throughout the camping areas (more added for 2026!). All bathrooms will be serviced daily. If you notice an issue, please visit Guest Services or email us at realperson@hinterlandiowa.com.

Showers will be available for purchase for $10 (credit card only). Showers are located just east of Dollar General along the festival trail.

Shower Hours (Thursday-Sunday): 6 AM–12 PM and 3 PM–9 PM

topics.title: Allowed/Not Allowed - Campgrounds
topics.body:
Every person, vehicle and belonging entering the festival or camp grounds is subject to a full airport-style search, which may include a magnetometer screening and/or pat-down.

These items are NOT allowed in campgrounds:

NO weapons of any kind
NO pyro stuff (No tiki torches, fireworks or the like, please)
NO glass
NO pets (service animals are welcome, see policy)
NO selling stuff, unlicensed vending, sponsor tents
NO swimming in the pond
NO vehicles in Tent Campgrounds
NO RVs in regular parking lots
NO motorized bicycles, scooters, etc.

These items ARE allowed in campgrounds:

YES food
YES small campfire stoves/grills that run on propane or charcoal
YES drinks with a limit of three cases of either beer, boxes of wine, or liquor bottles per campsite
YES firepits
YES bicycles
YES wagons for transporting gear

Please note that other items may be deemed prohibited at event organizers discretion.

Generators: Non-fuel generators are allowed in all campgrounds. Gas or diesel generators are not allowed in tent camping or car camping, but are allowed in both RV campgrounds.

topics.title: Power Access
topics.body:
Power is not provided for campers. Please plan accordingly.

The only exception is that Glamping and Powered RV Campsites. Glamping includes a power strip with 20-amp service. Powered RV Campsites include a 50-amp power hookup. Bring your own adapter if your RV uses a 30-amp connection. They will not be available for sale.

topics.title: Food, Drink, Ice & Water
topics.body:
Campground Food & Drink Vendors
We'll have delicious food & drink available for purchase in Basecamp.

Outside Food & Drink
You're welcome to bring your own food and drink into the campgrounds. We have a limit of three cases of either beer, boxes of wine, or liquor bottles per group. Please keep glass bottles at home. No outside food or drinks are allowed within the festival grounds, only the campgrounds.

Water
We'll have water refill stations throughout all the campgrounds and within the festival grounds. We encourage you to bring refillable water bottles or jugs.

Ice
Ice will be available for purchase in Basecamp and Car Camping.

Camp Stoves
Small campfire stoves/grills that run on propane or charcoal are permitted.

topics.title: What's Considered an RV
topics.body:
Every RV entering the festival grounds requires an RV Campsite pass and cannot park in any other area. The following vehicles are considered an RV.

- Any size RV (motorhome): Class A, Class B or Class C
- Any size bus (no tour buses, prevosts, or motorcoaches with low clearance allowed)
- Any vehicle wider or longer than a normal 15 passenger van (230 x 80 x 80)
- Any vehicle towing a camper or 5th wheel of any size.
- If you're hitching anything, it's an RV. (Box trucks and trailers are not allowed into the campgrounds.)

topics.title: Leaving the Campgrounds
topics.body:
All campers must exit the campgrounds by Monday at Noon.

Re-entry
Tent Camping Parking, Glamping Parking, RV Camping Companion Vehicles - re-entry ALLOWED during daylight hours

Car Camping, RV Camping - re-entry NOT ALLOWED

topics.title: RV Services
topics.body: New this year! Hinterland now offers one-time fresh water refill or pump out service during daylight hours for Powered and Non-Powered RV pass holders, for a fee. Services will be completed within 24 hours of purchase. Use this link or scan the QR codes onsite to request a service. Please provide your RV lot number and a description of your RV so our service team can locate you. You can also combine the services for a discount!

topics.title: Single Day Camping
topics.body: Camping passes cover all four days of the festival. If you are attending for less than four days, you are still welcome to camp. Just purchase the camping pass type of your choice!
